municipal_cultural_relics.use: Confirms the date and address range independently of the photograph descriptions.

images.author: Fayhoo
images.observation: Two separate structures are visible. At image left the bowed stone rail, closely turned spindles, a dentil cornice, central pier with round ornament and the top of one column appear above garden foliage. The face of the other building has a different opening and balcony pattern.

images.author: MNXANL
images.observation: The same curved parapet and distinctive central roundel, projecting bracket, narrow cap and line of separate dentils reappear toward image left. The picture includes the contemporary office entrance, which is outside this model.

archived_image_search.conclusion: No early image independently identifying this exact balustrade was confirmed. The dated 2014 and 2019 photographs establish the exterior as documented in that period.

attribution.claim: The secondary history identifies the pair as the residences of the Kwok brothers of Wing On. The original municipal name and the domestic origin of the site are preserved separately.

model_limits: The single photo-matched curved segment and one visible upper column section are modeled. The garden plants hide the remainder of the column; the lower end is a cut surface.

The two buildings share a registered address range. The western assignment and a particular brother/house number are not confirmed separately, so this detail is identified by its photographic features.
No original measured drawing has yet been located for this part. Curvature, span, height, interrupted railing repetitions, lower profile and materials are estimated.
The Shanghai Exhibition Centre occupies the site of a distinct former garden across the street. Its architecture and the modern government office entrance are outside the study.
